body:
For a startup, a strong brand identity is not just nice to have.

It helps investors, customers and new hires understand what you do before they have time to read the details.

I’ve refreshed this list for 2026, checking every agency’s current website for location, pricing, timeline, past work and contact details.

The list runs from startup-focused studios to some of the world’s best-known firms, and ends with my own practice as a solo alternative, so you can compare them by budget and stage.

10 branding agencies for startups

  1. Bolder
  2. The Branx
  3. Ramotion
  4. Wolff Olins
  5. Pentagram
  6. Motto
  7. Mucho
  8. Clay
  9. Further (formerly DesignStudio)
  10. Ebaqdesign

1. Bolder

Bolder describes itself as the agency that brands “the companies that are hardest to explain.”

Bolder work page. Image source.

It focuses on AI, robotics, biotech, energy and deep tech, where the product is often harder to explain than to build.

The work page opens with a 3D render of the Alicia robot, labeled with real specs like torque and cleaning area.

I like that approach, because it turns technical detail into the visual language instead of hiding it.

The Acorn biotech identity takes another route, with wide monospaced type over a textured, microscope-like surface.

Bolder also publishes its prices, which is rare: pre-seed and seed projects start at $15,000 and take two to eight weeks.

Location: San Francisco, New York, Berlin and London
Timeline: 2–8 weeks for pre-seed and seed; 6–16 weeks for Series A and later
Price: From $15,000 for early-stage branding and websites; $35,000–$200,000 for Series A to IPO
Past work: Alicia, Acorn Biolabs, Attero, Brightly
Contact: Project form; they reply within 24 hours

View Bolder’s work.

2. The Branx

The Branx calls itself the tech branding agency for AI and SaaS startups.

The Branx work page. Image source.

The team of nine says it has built more than 120 tech brands across the US, Canada, the UK and Europe.

Its portfolio is clean and product-led, with marks that work well as app icons and on dark interfaces.

I like the Dablam symbol, a circle cut by vertical strokes, set against a glowing mountain ridge.

The Eluviant wordmark is another strong example: stacked horizontal lines suggest motion and video without any literal camera icon.

Pricing is published too, with a brand identity from €20,000 in about three weeks.

Location: Spain (The Branx Europe S.L.); works across the US, Canada, the UK and the EU
Timeline: About 3 weeks for brand identity; about 6 weeks with a website
Price: From €20,000 for brand identity; from €35,000 with a 5-page website
Past work: Metricool, Furanova, Dablam, Eluviant, Featherless, North, docStribute, Causaly
Contact: hi@thebranx.com or the project form

View The Branx’s work.

3. Ramotion

Ramotion is a brand and digital product agency with offices in San Francisco, Los Angeles and New York.

Ramotion work page. Image source.

It runs dedicated programs for startups, with branding, web design and UX under one roof.

The client list is unusually strong for a mid-sized studio: Firefox, Salesforce, Stripe, Netflix and Descript all appear on its work page.

I like how the Firefox posters use bright gradients and bold slogans to make privacy feel energetic rather than technical.

That mix of brand and product design is useful for startups whose app is the brand.

Pricing isn’t published, so expect to discuss budget on a first call.

Location: 28 Geary St, San Francisco; also Los Angeles and New York
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; quoted per project
Past work: Firefox, Salesforce, Clearbit, Turo, Netflix, Citrix, Descript, Stripe, Volusion, Okta
Contact: newbusiness@ramotion.com or +1 415 831 7880

View Ramotion’s work.

4. Wolff Olins

Wolff Olins is a global brand consultancy that works “from global icons to trailblazing start-ups.”

Wolff Olins work page. Image source.

It is best known for big identities like Uber, TikTok and Lloyds, but its recent work also includes fast-growing challengers.

The Blank Street coffee identity is a good example, with a bright green, hand-painted-style sign that feels local despite rapid expansion.

Patreon’s shift from membership model to creator company is another startup-to-scale-up story in the portfolio.

I would consider Wolff Olins for a well-funded company at a defining moment, such as a major raise or category change.

Earlier versions of this article mentioned a dedicated startup division, but I couldn’t find one on its current site.

Location: London, New York, San Francisco and Los Angeles
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; enterprise-level budgets
Past work: Blank Street, Patreon, Decathlon, Benefit, Lloyds, Hyundai Card, LG, TikTok, Uber
Contact: clientsnewyork@wolffolins.com or clientslondon@wolffolins.com

View Wolff Olins’s work.

5. Pentagram

Pentagram is one of the world’s best-known design firms, run by independent partners in New York, London, Austin and Berlin.

Pentagram work page. Image source.

Its motto is “we design everything for everyone,” and the work covers technology and finance as well as arts and culture.

The latest projects show its typographic range: the BFI London Film Festival identity, a 40th-anniversary mark for MTA Arts & Design and the Storefront Gala.

I like how each identity is built around one strong typographic idea rather than a generic symbol.

For a startup, the advantage is working directly with a senior partner and their team.

The trade-off is budget, so Pentagram suits founders who see the identity as a long-term asset.

Location: 250 Park Avenue South, New York; also London, Austin and Berlin
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; quoted per project
Past work: BFI London Film Festival, MTA Arts & Design, Storefront for Art and Architecture
Contact: newyork@pentagram.com or +1 212 683 7000

View Pentagram’s work.

6. Motto

Motto is a strategic branding agency for technology and innovation companies at defining moments of growth.

Archival screenshot of Motto’s website. Image source.

It is best known for its “Ideas Worth Rallying Around” approach, which puts purpose and positioning before visuals.

Its listed clients include Microsoft, Google, Disney, Andela, Goodnotes, Prolific and Klaviyo.

That makes Motto a strong fit for startups whose biggest problem is the story, not the logo.

Clutch lists a minimum project size of $100,000, so it is best for well-funded teams.

Motto’s website blocks automated visits, so the image above is from an earlier capture.

Location: New York, London, Berlin and Dallas
Timeline: Not published
Price: Minimum project size of $100,000+ (Clutch)
Past work: Microsoft, Google, Disney, Andela, Goodnotes, Prolific, Klaviyo
Contact: Contact form on Motto’s website

View Motto’s work.

7. Mucho

Mucho is an independent design studio with offices in San Francisco and Barcelona.

Mucho work page. Image source.

It works across strategy, brand identity, websites, packaging and environments.

The portfolio mixes cultural clients like MACBA with startups such as Biotic and Eko Health.

I like the Biotic identity, where a dense dotted circle suggests a biological process without a literal leaf or cell.

Mucho’s strength is craft and range, from bold editorial type to playful packaging like Baby Bites.

That makes it a good fit for consumer and health startups that need a brand to work in print and in person, not just on screens.

Location: 466 Geary Street, San Francisco; Carrer Rosselló 47A, Barcelona
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; quoted per project
Past work: Biotic, Eko Health, Alianza, MACBA, Art Gallery of NSW, Baby Bites, Krateo Sky
Contact: sanfrancisco@wearemucho.com, +1 415 546 1399, or barcelona@wearemucho.com

View Mucho’s work.

8. Clay

Clay is a remote-first UX design and branding agency headquartered in San Francisco.

Clay work page. Image source.

It is strongest in digital product and web design, with clients including Meta, Google, Stripe and Coinbase.

Earlier versions of this article credited Clay with Snapchat and Slack branding, but its site describes that work as UX design for Snapchat and web design for Slack.

Its brand identities are still worth a look, like the bold radiating gradient for the DeFi platform Sky.

I would choose Clay for a startup whose product experience matters as much as its logo.

Location: San Francisco; also New York, Austin, Denver, Lisbon and Belgrade
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; quoted per project
Past work: Meta, Google, Slack (web), Snapchat (UX), Coinbase, Stripe, Discover, Credit Karma, Marqeta, Sky
Contact: hey@clay.global or +1 415 796 6262

View Clay’s work.

9. Further (formerly DesignStudio)

Further is the new name of DesignStudio, the agency behind the famous Airbnb rebrand.

Further work page. Image source.

It still has a collection called “Branding Unicorns”, featuring Airbnb, Deliveroo and GetYourGuide.

The newer work is just as bold, from the Wimbledon identity to a high-energy look for rugby’s HSBC SVNS series.

I like the Eurostar rebrand in particular, where a star-like spark becomes a livery graphic across the whole train.

Further is a good fit for startups preparing for a global launch or IPO, where the brand has to work at a very large scale.

Location: London (12–16 Clerkenwell Road), New York (300 Kent Avenue, Brooklyn) and Dubai
Timeline: Not published
Price: Not published; quoted per project
Past work: Airbnb, Deliveroo, GetYourGuide, Eurostar, Wimbledon, Depop, EA Sports, HSBC SVNS
Contact: newyork@further.group or london@further.group

View Further’s work.

10. Ebaqdesign

Ebaqdesign is my own practice in New York, and it isn’t a typical multi-person agency: I work as a solo branding expert, so founders deal with the senior designer directly, not an account team.

Ebaqdesign homepage. Image source.

I’m Arek Dvornechuck, a Branding Expert with over 20 years of experience.

Before starting my own practice, I worked with leading design firms, including Chermayeff & Geismar & Haviv.

Most startups I work with need to look established before a raise, a launch or their first enterprise sale.

A scoped brand identity or rebrand starts at one week for $3,000: logo system, colors, typography and practical guidelines.

Larger scopes, such as a website, motion or a full brand system, take extra weeks at the same weekly rate.

For recent examples, see Periti Digital, Savory and the Airport Executive rebrand.

Location: New York City; solo branding expert working with clients worldwide
Timeline: 1 week+ (one week for a scoped identity; more weeks for larger scopes)
Price: $3,000 per week
Past work: Periti Digital, Savory, Airport Executive, Orbio, NextDim AI, Elevate, Lyntics
Contact: Book a call

Discuss your startup brand with Arek.

Choosing the right agency for your startup

When you compare agencies, I would look at five things.

  1. Portfolio alignment: look for work in your industry, or at least for companies at your stage.
  2. Budget fit: published prices range from $3,000 to six figures, so shortlist agencies you can actually afford.
  3. Scalability: make sure the identity is a system, with guidelines and files your team can use without the agency.
  4. Who does the work: ask whether you’ll work with senior designers or be handed to a junior team.
  5. Timeline: check that the agency can deliver before your raise, launch or demo day.

Which agencies specialize in tech startup branding?

From this list, Bolder focuses on deep tech such as AI, robotics, biotech and energy.

The Branx focuses on AI and SaaS startups, and Ramotion and Clay combine branding with product and web design.

If you’re still researching, see my articles on tech startup logos, SaaS logos and the brand strategy framework for startups.

Best logo design agencies for early-stage startups

At pre-seed or seed, you usually need a credible logo and identity system quickly, not a six-month brand program.

Three options on this list publish prices that suit that stage: Bolder from $15,000, The Branx from €20,000 and, as a solo option, Ebaqdesign from $3,000 for one week.

If speed matters most, you can also compare 13 branding agencies that deliver in one week.

Pricing considerations

Only four of these ten agencies publish their prices, but those four show the range clearly.

  • Solo branding expert: $3,000 per week, from one week for an identity (Ebaqdesign).
  • Startup-focused studios: about $15,000–€35,000 for identity, or identity plus website (Bolder, The Branx).
  • Established agencies: $35,000–$200,000 for full brand building (Bolder’s Series A to IPO range).
  • Global consultancies: six figures and up, such as Motto’s $100,000+ minimum on Clutch.

Investing in professional branding early can save a costly rebrand later and help attract investment, customers and talent.
